name: Jim McKelvey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Jim McKelvey cofounded payments firm Square with Jack Dorsey in 2009 after he had trouble selling a $2,000 art piece from his studio; the company was renamed Block in 2021.
McKelvey remains on Block's board He started a new company, Invisibly, which powers micropayments for journalism and publishing.
He owns nearly 5% of Block stock and has netted at least $270 million from selling Block shares over the years.
A serial entrepreneur, he has started at least seven companies, ranging from a CD cabinet maker to a glass-blowing studio.
He also sits on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and started a nonprofit, LaunchCode, to teach people how to program.
In March 2020, he released "The Innovation Stack," a book detailing Square's battle with Amazon to create a better payments system.
forbes_facts: McKelvey is the author of two textbooks on computer science and one textbook called "The Art Of Fire: Beginning Glassblowing."
He hired Jack Dorsey as a teenager to be an engineering intern for his first tech company, Mira.

name: Girdhari Jaisinghani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun India (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: The eldest of five siblings, Girdhari Jaisinghani owns a minority stake in listed Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
The company was started in 1986 by his younger brother Inder as a trading firm.
Today, Polycab gets the bulk of its revenues from wires and cables.
It supplies everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fiber cables. Its customers are largely in the oil and gas, power and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
forbes_facts: He has no executive role in the company.

name: Stanley Hubbard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Veteran media mogul Stanley Hubbard helms Hubbard Broadcasting, which owns 13 TV stations and 57 radio stations across the U.S.
Founded by Hubbard's father in 1925, the Minnesota-based company has expanded its portfolio to include cable network Reelz.
Hubbard grew up in the family business, working as prop person at 17, a photojournalist in college and later moving into management.
forbes_facts: Hubbard played hockey for the University of Minnesota.
Hubbard's father founded the first commercial TV station in Minnesota; he also bought the first TV camera ever sold, in 1938.

name: Jahm Najafi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Jahm Najafi is a Phoenix-based private equity investor whose portfolio includes direct-to-consumer brands and minority stakes in sports teams.
An Iranian by birth, Najfi's family immigrated to the U.S. when he was a child.
After a stint on Wall Street and his older brother's Pivotal Group real estate firm, Najafi launched his own investment firm, Najafi Companies.
His most lucrative acquisition was a $100 million bet in 2003 on domain registrar Network Solutions, which he sold for $800 million in 2007.
Najafi acquired 10% of the Phoenix Suns in 2009 and rolled forward his stake when a group led by billionaire Mat Ishbia bought the team for $4 billion in 2023.
forbes_facts: Najafi previously owned a minority stake in British Formula 1 team McLaren Racing, which he sold in a 2025 deal that valued McLaren at $4.5 billion.
Najafi's MSP Sports Capital has invested in several European football clubs alongside billionaire Blackstone executive David Blitzer.

name: Ulrich Mommert
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Ulrich Mommert took over Austrian lighting company ZKW In 1982, when it was on the brink of bankruptcy.
He refocused ZKW on lighting technology for high-end automobiles, with clients such as BMW, Mercedes, Porsche and Audi.
In 2018 Mommert sold the company to South Korean firm LG for $1.2 billion.
Mommert owns a horse racing team and a trotting track in Berlin-Mariendorf.
forbes_facts: He used to be an amateur horse racer, and won more than 160 races; he is believed to own around 100 horses.

name: Ludwig Theodor Braun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025)
forbes_bio: Ludwig Theodor Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
His father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Ludwig Theodor is the youngest son of Ludwig Georg. His sister Anna Maria is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
forbes_facts: B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Andrei Komarov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025)
forbes_bio: In March 2021, Komarov sold his 87% stake in Chelyabinsk Tube Rolling Plant, also known as ChelPipe, one of Russia's leading steel pipe makers to the fellow billionaire Dmitry Pumpyansky for $1.13 bil
He managed Moscow's Satiricon Theater in the last years of communism.
He traded cars, metal products and steel pipes in the early 1990s.
In the mid-90s, in his hometown of Chelyabinsk, he teamed up with the manager of the town's pipe-making plant to private the business.
forbes_facts: Komarov is a Harley-Davidson motorcycle fan.

name: Trey Parker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Trey Parker and his creative partner Matt Stone debuted the foul-mouthed cartoon comedy "South Park" in 1997, writing, producing and voicing more than 300 episodes and counting.

In 2007, Parker and Stone struck a deal with Comedy Central to split the then-non-existent digital revenues for their show 50-50 "in perpetuity," minting them a fortune as streaming revolutionized the TV landscape.
They are also the co-creators of the hit musical "The Book of Mormon," which has been performed on Broadway more than 5,000 times since 2011 and toured around the world.
In July 2025, the pair renewed their deal with Paramount Skydance to create new episodes of "South Park" and payout their half of the digital revenues for an estimated $250 million per year.

name: Apoorva Mehta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2023)
forbes_bio: Apoorva Mehta is a cofounder of San Francisco-based grocery delivery firm Instacart, which went public on the Nasdaq under its legal name Maplebear in 2023.
Mehta served as chairman and CEO for nearly a decade after cofounding the company in 2012. He stepped down as CEO in 2021 and chairman in 2023.
He still owns about 7% of Maplebear's common stock plus options to acquire another 1% of the company.
In 2022, private investors valued Mehta's new health-tech startup Cloud Health Systems at $200 million.
Born in India, Mehta lived in Libya before moving to Canada, where he eventually studied engineering at the University of Waterloo.
forbes_facts: Before founding Instacart, Mehta tried to create a product focused on social networking for lawyers.
In Instacart's early days, orders often came in without a shopper available, so Mehta, who did not own a car, made the deliveries himself via Uber.

name: Madeleine Olsson Eriksson
name_chinese: 马德琳·奥尔森·埃里克森
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2014-2021); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Madeleine Olsson-Eriksson is a part owner of Stena Sphere, a privately held Swedish conglomerate.
Interests include cruising, shipping, offshore drilling, property and metal recycling.
Madeleine's father, Sten, founded Stena in 1939 as a trading company.
Her brother Dan took over in 1983 and now owns 51% of the company. Madeleine and her brother Stefan Olsson own 12.5% and 24.5%, respectively.
Madeleine's children, Gustav and Marie, each own 6%  and have seats on different boards in the company.
forbes_facts: She became the first of her family to go to college, earning a degree in medicine and pursuing a career as a gynecologist.
Aside from an 12.5% stake in Stena, she is also part owner of a clinic in Gothenburg.
